The Quest

Ten pieces, one Round 1 submission

Follow these in order. Every step needs the whole team on the same page before you move to the next — that's how HCL Jigsaw checks you're really working together, not just one teammate racing ahead.

1
Step 1 · Get In

Log in to your account

Head to hcljigsaw.hyrenet.in/login and sign in with the Username and Secret Password your school coordinator handed your team. This one login is shared by the whole team for all of Round 1.

Coach's noteSave this login somewhere every teammate can reach — you'll land back on this exact screen every time you check in on your team's progress.
2
Step 2 · Find Round 1

Open the Activities tab

On the Students Dashboard, look at the sidebar on the left and click Activities. This is home base for every round of Jigsaw 7.0, including the Round 1 challenge your team is starting now.

Coach's noteWatch the Progress ring at the top right — it's sitting at 0 / 1 right now. Everything in this guide is what moves it to 1.
3
Step 3 · Open The Activity

Choose your challenge

Tap the Round 1 Activity card to expand it. Two sub-levels show up — Choose Your Challenge and Team Worksheet. Click into Choose Your Challenge first; the worksheet stays locked (and shows no checkmark) until your theme is settled.

Coach's note"Tap to expand" and "Tap to collapse" are the same card — you're just opening and closing the same two sub-levels as you move through them.
4
Step 4 · Decide As A Team

Read the rules, then pick a theme

Before anyone taps a challenge, read the guidelines that pop up. The rule that matters most: your team selects and completes only one theme for Round 1.

  • Theme selection — choose any one challenge for your submission.
  • Flexible selection — whoever picked it can change it, until every teammate approves.
  • Problem statement view — unlocks for everyone only once the whole team has approved.
Coach's noteTalk it through as a group before anyone taps approve. Once everyone says yes, that theme's problem statement is what your worksheet gets judged against.
5
Step 5 · Unlock The Worksheet

Head back to the Team Worksheet

Once every teammate has approved the same theme, go back into Activities and open the second sub-level: Team Worksheet. This is where your team's real work gets written down.

Coach's noteLook for the checkmark next to Choose Your Challenge — that's your confirmation the whole team's approval actually went through.
6
Step 6 · Know The Rules

Read how the worksheet submission works

Any one teammate can submit the worksheet — but everyone else has to approve it. Want to swap in a better file after someone's already submitted? Upload the new one; it needs fresh approval from the whole team too.

  • Step 1 — download the Group Worksheet template.
  • Step 2 — read and understand every question in it.
  • Step 3 — answer the questions and save the file.
  • Step 4 — upload the filled worksheet with Submit Worksheet.
Coach's noteOne submitter, one team decision. If two teammates upload two different files, only the version everyone approves is the one that counts.
7
Step 7 · Do The Work

Download, answer, and save

Tap Download Worksheet Template, open it, and work through every question together — the template already carries your team's approved problem statement on the cover slide. Save the file once every question has a real answer.

Coach's noteSplit the questions across the team so no one's staring at a blank slide alone — research questions first, writing and design questions last. See exactly what a filled template looks like below.
8
Step 8 · Lock The Format

Get team approval, then Save As PDF

Once every teammate has reviewed and approved the finished worksheet, open the file and use Save As → PDF. The upload box only accepts a PDF — not the original PowerPoint file.

Coach's noteA PDF locks your formatting exactly where you left it — what your team approved is exactly what your mentors will see.
9
Step 9 · Upload It

Choose the file and submit

Back on the Team Worksheet screen, tap Choose File, select your saved PDF, and send it in. Keep it under the 10 MB limit.

Coach's noteSame Choose File button from Step 6 — give the file a quick once-over before you tap it, typos are easier to catch now than after submitting.
10
Step 10 · Final Approval

Everyone approves, then you wait

Every teammate approves the submitted worksheet. Once it's unanimous, your Round 1 submission is locked in — and it's just a wait for Round 2 from here.

Coach's noteYour dashboard progress won't hit 100% until that last approval lands — don't let a submission sit unapproved in the team chat.
What "Done" Looks Like

A real problem statement, start to finish

This is an actual Round 1 brief — the Grade 9, AI Revolution & Digital Futures theme called UPI Fraud Awareness Assistant — shown exactly as your team would see it once everyone approves a theme in Step 4, and exactly what the worksheet from Step 7 asks you to fill in.

Grade 9 · AI Revolution & Digital Futures

UPI Fraud Awareness Assistant

Team Worksheet · work through this together as a group

The Story

UPI scams are rising fast in India. Most people know how to use UPI but don't know the common tricks scammers use. Your team is building a chatbot that helps people spot these tricks before they lose money.

Your Challenge

Design a chatbot that helps people recognise common UPI fraud tricks and stay safe, before they lose money. This worksheet covers research, ideation, and design.

A researched list of fraud tricks & red flags A documented chatbot conversation design A pitch & safety poster for your assistant
Q1

Research and document 5 common UPI fraud tricks from news articles or police advisories. For each: the fraud's name, how it works in simple steps, and one red flag to spot it.

Q2

Find 2–3 real statistics about UPI fraud in India (how common it is, how much money is lost), and cite where you found them. Then name 2 emotions or tricks scammers use — think fear, urgency, greed, or trust.

Q3

Talk to 2 people about their UPI experience. Have they seen a suspicious message or call? What happened? Write what each person said, and their age or relation to you.

Q4

Find out what NPCI, a bank, or the police have already done to warn people about UPI fraud. What's missing? A quick web search for "UPI safety campaign" is a good start.

Q5

Compare 2 free chatbot-building tools (like ManyChat, Tidio, or Landbot) — which is easier for your team to use, and why? Then draw or describe a simple flowchart (4–5 boxes): user describes a situation → chatbot asks a question → chatbot decides if it's a scam → chatbot gives a warning.

Q6

Pick 1 fraud type and write the full conversation: what the user says, what the chatbot asks, and what warning it gives — make it sound natural, not robotic. What should the chatbot say if the situation isn't actually a scam? It should reassure without sounding dismissive.

Q7

Write your chatbot's opening message. Keep it short, friendly, and clear about what it does. Then write 2 warning messages for 2 different fraud types; each should clearly say it's a scam, explain why, and tell the person what to do. Be clear and calm — not scary or preachy.

Q8

Sketch a simple safety poster for WhatsApp with your top 5 UPI safety rules. Think about what would make someone actually stop and read it. Upload a photo of your sketch — hand-drawn is fine.

Q9

Plan how you'll test your chatbot with 5 real people over a few days. Who will you ask? Then write how you'll measure if they learned something: 2–3 simple before/after questions, asked the same or similar way both times.

Q10

Write your pitch: the problem, your chatbot solution, and what you're asking a school or the police to do. End with a clear, specific ask.

Before You Start

Keep these in mind as a team

The four things that trip teams up most often in Round 1 — worth a quick check before the deadline gets close.

1

Only one theme. Your team selects and completes a single challenge for Round 1 — not one per member.

2

Everyone approves, every time. The theme, and the worksheet, each need every teammate's sign-off before they're final.

3

PDF only. The worksheet upload accepts a completed, saved-as-PDF file — max 10 MB.

4

Blank or incomplete gets removed. Make sure every question has a real, thought-through answer before submitting.
